utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning, sir. Would you please take the card in your hand and read aloud the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you hear me being translated into your language.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness does not have his microphone on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm hearing from the interpreters they could not hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that, too, but I heard the witness. We must now switch on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're asked a minute or two while some technical problem is resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The technical problem in the Macedonian booth has now been corrected so we may proceed. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, at the outset, I would like to ask for the assistance of the usher to show you a pieces of paper. And could you please, without stating any information on the piece of paper, can you tell us whether that piece of paper contains your true name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, before you go away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is the other information on that piece of paper correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we move into private session just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, today, I will address you by the number M-037, and so can you please try not to mention your own name or other information that might identify you in public session. When it is necessary, we will move into private session. Have you lived your entire life in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask that the witness moves closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you see if you could improve the position of the microphone, please, Mr. Court Officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is your ethnicity Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you a professional police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In your years of service as a police officer, have you always performed your duties to the best of your ability?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you an active police officer during the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During that time of crisis in Macedonia, at times, did you risk your life to protect the lives and safety of the citizens of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, are police officers in Macedonia part of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are police officers in Macedonia part of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a number of exhibits to show to the witness today, and we brought a few binders with tabbed hard copies for the assistance of the Judges, if the usher could distribute them, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, there is no need to show the witness anything right now. Hopefully, we will be able to use the e-court system; but if not, I'm grateful, because then we will turn to that binder. If we could show the witness what is on tab 1, which is 65 ter number 99.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I mention, Mr. Saxon, that the identification sheet has not --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- got past the witness at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I apologise, Your Honour. Could that identification sheet be tendered into the record, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could it first be shown to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, please. And the Prosecution would be grateful if this could be tendered under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, if you take a look at the computer screen in front of you, you see that it's a split screen, and you can see a document in Macedonian on the right-hand side and the English translation on the left-hand side. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we lose it, the identification sheet will be received under seal, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P32, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the two versions of the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd ask to you follow along, please, in the version that is in your language. This document is titled, "Rules on the organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior." Do you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just briefly, if we look at Article 1, it says: "These rules establish the internal organisation of the Ministry of Interior; henceforth, the Ministry, excluding the security and counter-intelligence division." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then Article 2, the very first line: "The Minister of the Interior; henceforth, the Minister, is in charge of the work of the Ministry of Interior." And the last sentence of Article 2 reads: "The Public Security Bureau as an organ of the Ministry is headed by a director." Are you still following me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then below, there's a subtitle part 2, called, "Internal Organisation," and we see Article 3, which reads: "For the completion of the work of the Public Security Bureau, two departments are founded; the police department and the criminal police department, as well as other autonomous organisational systems." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that is followed by Article 4, which says: "The police performs work that is directly concerned with the maintenance of public law and order, the regulation and control of traffic on the roads, the control of state border crossings, the protection of certain individuals and buildings," and then it goes on, "as well as other work established in Article 1 of the law on Internal Affairs, which by nature or conditions require that it be performed by uniformed employees of the Ministry." Do you see what I've just read?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And does that description of the police accord with your knowledge and experience as a professional police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could, with the Court officer's assistance move to the next page, please, in each version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Witness M-037, you see there is an article called Article 9. Do you see that article?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Was that a yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Article 9 begins: "Internal affairs sector for the city of Skopje is organised along the following internal organisational systems." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for us what is meant by the term "internal affairs sector" within the organisation of the police and Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Are you referring to the sector for Internal Affairs of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes. But I'm asking in general what does a -- the term "sector" mean within the organisation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I would not be able to explain to you that as an expert because as you can see the sector, there are many more units where, for instance, the Department of Analytics, sector for aliens, where usually it is the uniformed police officer who were aware that such sectors exist, but they don't have anything to do with those sectors. The uniformed police officers work only on the tasks of maintenance of public order and peace. With the redeployment by the Minister or person authorised by them, a uniformed officer could work with one of these departments or sectors, but could I not explain what a sector is as an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am seeing from Mr. Tarculovski that apparently is he not receiving translation or interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could that matter be checked? It would appear that neither accused is receiving translation. Thank you for letting us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TARCULOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only hear the translation. But when the witness is speaking, we cannot hear that through the earphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It appears the problem is now resolved. One of the consequences perhaps of moving courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn to the very last page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn to the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Witness M-037 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-037, if you take a look at the bottom of that last page, you see a stamp and the words, "Ministry of the Interior, Dosta Dimovska." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the date, "26 January 2001, Skopje." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just briefly, can you tell us who became Minister of the Interior after Dosta Dimovska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I think it was the Minister, Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm going to perhaps move slightly out of the order of the exhibits that are in your binders. If we can show the photo that is actually in tab 20, please, which was Prosecution Exhibit P15, and this is actually from page 23 of the court binder, photo A.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the uniforms depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recognise these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, in 2001 who, if anyone, was wearing these kinds of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: These were worn by the uniformed part of the police; the reserve force, the special officers, and the special police unit. At that period, almost all police officers that were to -- that were going in the field were wearing camouflage uniforms if we had them, because it happened at one time when there was a shortage of camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us what the insignia on the sleeves that are in the foreground of the photograph say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: "Police." That's on the right sleeve, and on the left is the emblem of the police. That is on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could now look at what you have at tab 21, which is 65 ter number 199.17. It is photograph B on page 23 of the court binder that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, before we move on to discuss the next photograph, I need to clarify something that you told us just a moment ago. You said that these camouflage uniforms were worn by the uniformed part of the police; the reserve force, the special officers, and the special police unit. What do you mean by the "uniformed part of the police"? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Uniformed part of the police? Well, all the things from maintaining the public order are under the uniformed police and, usually, uniforms are worn at the time, except for in special situation when the police is wearing civilian clothes in order not to be recognised when certain special tasks or actions are being performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you refer to the uniformed police, are you referring to professional police officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: When I speak about the uniformed police, I think that we are talking about this period 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I think of the professional police officers and the reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at the photograph that you now see in front of you, these are patches on camouflage uniforms. Can you read to us what these patches say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: "Republic of Macedonia, Police."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, in August of 2001, did you and your colleagues wear such patches on your uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you mean both photographs, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The prior photograph is already in evidence as P15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So I would seek to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P35, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness 37, after receiving your orders on that morning, on the 12th of August, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: After we received the order, the team that was listed in the order, we went to the checkpoints Straista, I think it was called, and that's where we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately, how far from the village of Ljuboten is this Straista check-point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: This is quite an extensive question. I cannot tell you anything specific. Do you think about the first house? Maybe you think about the fields that are in the vicinity of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise. My question should have been clearer. Approximately, for example, how far would this check-point be, say, from the mosque at the centre of Ljuboten, roughly? How many kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Maybe around one kilometre, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And from this spot, were you able to observe the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you using your binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall, roughly, more or less, what time did you arrive at this check-point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I think it was around 8.00 or 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you arrived at this check-point, did you receive any information about what was happening in the village of Ljuboten at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. I think until 7.00, according to the work order, Mihajlo Dusko was at work and (redacted) from him, and I took it there at the spot because I think that's where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must now adjourn for the first break and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with great respect, could the Chamber instruct the witness not to discuss his evidence during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why is that necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I know that the witness has not one but two mobile phone calls with him, and it is possible he may receive a phone call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will understand, sir, that during your evidence, you should not discuss your witness with any other person, that is any person that you meet or by telephone or any other means. If you could observe that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we still in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is necessary to adjourn for five or ten minutes. We must do that and if the witness could be escorted immediately from the courtroom. --- Break taken at 11.47 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We now continue, Mr. Saxon. We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that you saw three bodies. Do you know how these three persons died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Do I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: No. I assume that it was the shooting that I saw previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know who shot these three people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: There was a small group of people who were by the road. I suppose it was them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you be a bit more specific. Do you know where these people came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Do you mean the murdered people?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No. I mean the people who were shooting near the side of the road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: That was the group of uniformed people who have entered after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "who have entered," do you mean who have entered the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. I'm referring to those who entered the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry that we were delayed coming in to court. We are still trying to resolve some technical problems with e-court and documents that should not go public, and I think there had been discussions with counsel and we're gradually working out a procedure that will be to the minimum inconvenience of counsel but will allow as much as possible to go to the outside world. Before we continue with the witness, we need for the record to receive as an exhibit and have marked, firstly, the facts that have been agreed as not in dispute between the Prosecution and the accused, Mr. Boskoski. These were actually submitted in December of last year to the Chamber; and, secondly, facts that have been agreed as not in dispute between the Prosecution and Mr. Tarculovski, and that those facts are in a document submitted on the 1st of February of this year. So we will have those incorporated as two separate exhibits in the record of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P43 and P44, respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon. You now feel you have entirely spent your interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So to speak, Your Honour. I believe it's time now for the start of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, I'm sorry to have delayed you this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examination by Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. M-037. I'm Edina Residovic; and together with my co-counsel Guenael Mettraux, I represent Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I move on to my questions, Mr. M-037, I would like to ask you to hear me out. I know that you understand the language that I speak, B/C/S, and I understand Macedonian, the language that you speak. You could answer all my questions very fast. However, my question and your answer have to be interpreted so that the Honourable Trial Chamber and our colleagues in the courtroom know what it is that I'm asking and what it is you're answering. So could you kindly pause before answering my question. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask for closed session, because of a few questions that have I in relation to the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Mirkovci police station, as you said, was within the municipality of Cair police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Within the department of the police of the municipality of Cair, the civilian police work was organised as well as the uniformed police work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the Cair department of the police, there is actually an operations section. That is the crime prevention police, and it employs policemen who usually work in civilian clothes. To put it very simply, they are engaged in the discovery of perpetrators of crimes, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is not called crime prevention but criminalistic police, as far I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that qualification. I think that would be a better way of putting it, too. In response to my colleague's question, you said that as for Cair, there were two police stations: Mirkovci and Cair. There was -- so there were two police stations. Is it true that after what happened in Ljuboten, was there a reserve police station set in Kucevishte in Ljubanci; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct that a reserve police station was established in Ljubanci, but I think that the premises of the reserve police station, Ljubanci, were located at the bus station, in the village. These used to be some municipal offices or something like a registrar's office of the village. Otherwise, the school housed -- there were rooms there for both of army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. You have already said but let us say that once again, that the immediate superior officer of all the employees in the police station was the commander of the police station, and then your superior was the head of the Interior in Cair; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. My direct superior was the commander and above him was the head, Ljube Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-037, that in actual fact the tasks and responsibilities of the police were set out in the law, primarily the law on the Interior, and in the field of crime, in the law on criminal procedure of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like the witness to be shown P33.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is the rule book regarding the organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior that was shown to you by my colleague the Prosecutor. A few moments ago you saw these rules. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. There is such a rule book.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could page 2 please displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before that, can we just set the record straight: You did recognise the seal and the signature of Dosta Dimovska, the Minister, who actually passed these rules; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, as the one shown before, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So you can agree with me that that is part of the Minister's work, to adopt general documents like the rules that we have right in front of us now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, the Minister has that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you now please look at Article 8 of these rules. It is right in front of you now. Is it correct that this Article establishes that in the area of the Republic of Macedonia, sectors of Internal Affairs are organised carrying out all police work in the territory of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Then I believe there were 11. Now the number will be reduced to 8 sectors or is yet to be reduced. I don't know what is the situation at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the city of Skopje, which is at the same time the capital of Macedonia and also the biggest city of Macedonia, precisely because of the large amount of work involving, the sector for the Interior is subdivided into departments of the Interior, in certain municipalities of that city. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This division of work in the city of Skopje in terms of these departments is also clearly shown in these rules from Article 13 through 17 on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this displayed, page 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-037, that in every department of the Interior, in individual municipalities in Skopje, there is a section for operations work, within which there is the crime investigation police, which carries out all police work, as for that particular line of police work. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. And I also think that in the hierarchy of things, the operational matters section has a greater importance than the police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All departments of the Interior in the city of Skopje also have the police stations mentioned in these rules. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you agree with me now, Mr. M-037, that in actual fact all the tasks and responsibilities carried out by the police either in accordance with the law on the Interior or the law on criminal procedure, that all these tasks and responsibilities are actually carried out within the sector of the Interior of the city of Skopje and the department of the Interior of the municipalities within the city of Skopje. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. M-037, that part of the employees of the Ministry of Interior in every department and every sector of the Interior are what is known as authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. Any person working in the department for Internal Affairs are authorised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You were an authorised official, too, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Just a bit of a clarification. We could not authorise the secretaries to the commanders and the technical staff. They are not authorised. Let's be clear about it. The remaining staff performing tasks in the area of public order and peace and other tasks set out in the law are authorised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. In actual fact all these authorised officials, regardless of whether working in crime investigation police or in the uniformed police, being authorised officials, they have the task, rights, and responsibilities directly stemming from the law. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And the answer to the previous question is yes, I was at that time authorised and I'm still an authorised officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you something different, Mr. M-037. If we look at these rules and the organisation of the sector of the Ministry of Interior of Skopje, we could see under number 1, that within the sector there was a duty operation centre that was organised. This centre -- this type of centre was organised in all other sectors of the Interior throughout the territory of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. In all sectors, there are duty operational centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If there is any suspicion regarding a fact or an event, in terms of the commission of a crime, you have already explained that the person, the policeman who would learn of such a fact should first report to the duty policeman in his own police station about that. Is that normal procedure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, it is the normal procedure and the hierarchy of the things would dictate such a procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: However, it would not be in contravention of the law if the policeman would distinctly inform, say, the duty investigating judge of the fact that he learned of something like that, that would not be in contravention of the law either, right? Though it is it not customary, although it is not the usual thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I don't know what is your purpose of mentioning the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps I should put question later, and then you will understand why it is that I'm referring to the investigating judge. Actually, could you tell me the following: The duty police officer at the police station, if he finds out about some facts that the policemen told him about, is he then the person who should inform the duty operation centre about what it is that you had just learned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is the most appropriate person for communication with the other services.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-037, that then the duty operations centre immediately notifies the investigating judge of the court that is in charge in relation of this fact that they learned of, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. The duty operation centre of the city of Skopje has, and that is the intention, to have coordination the other services in Skopje and in the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that once the police acts in this order, as you said, or rather that the duty operations centre informs the investigating judge that there is a suspicion that a particular fact could constitute a crime, that then all responsibilities are no longer set out by the police, but by the investigating judge who was informed about the said event. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: You're asking a very long question. I could not follow you with quality, and could not provide with a quality of responses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I do apologise. Let's take things one at a time. If a policeman sees as dead body in the street, you have already said that he informs his duty police officer at the police station about that, and then he in turn should inform the duty operation centre about that fact, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And besides that information line, he should also inform the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: According to the law, the duty operation centre, in respect of this fact if this is a crime or something that is suspected of having been a crime, has to inform the court, the judge. Is that the usual procedure in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is the usual procedure. The investigating judge is informed, and then they decide whether they would go at the scene of the crime or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. You have just given an answer to my previous question then. So now it is for the investigating judge to decide what will be done further. If you are following now, what I'm saying, could you please tell me whether you agree with this procedure: The investigating judge can decide not to go to the crime scene, and the judge can authorise the police to carry out the on-site investigation on their own. Is that one of the possibilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. They give us instructions for our further work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The investigating judge can, if the scene is far away from the premises of the court, can notify a judge from a court that is closer to the actual scene; and then this other investigating judge can go out to the crime scene. So can this other investigating judge become authorised in this way, in accordance with the law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I'm not really familiar with the competences the court has, but I suppose that this might happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The investigating judge can decide to go to the scene himself or herself and to carry out the on-site investigation; and then he, the investigating judge, sets up an investigation team that is supposed to carry out the investigation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, that is the regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In that situation, when the investigating judge decides to go to the scene himself or herself, then the police acts in accordance with the orders issued by the investigating judge and gives him the assistance that he seeks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. We assist them in the crime scene investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: None of the authorised officers can order the judge what he is going to do, once he comes to the scene, in terms of what he is going to do and how he is going to carry out the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. They have the undisputed right to decided with regard to the a specific act --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask that the speakers not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: According to the law of the Republic of Macedonia, it is only the investigating judge that can decide to have a post-mortem carried out on the bodies that were perhaps found on the premise or at the scene. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is only the investigating judge, but I know that the investigating judge can order a post-mortem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, all decisions as to whether how and when an investigation will be carried out at the scene are made by the investigating judge who was informed by the police in the first place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. And then they give us feedback about the decisions they have made about the event on which they were informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: As for the authorised officers in the police who are assisting the investigating judge, is it their duty only to compile an Official Note on what they had done, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: I'm not sure if they have the duty to compile an Official Note. I don't think this is their duty or obligation. If the judge would perform the crime scene investigation, it is our task to assist them, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just have a moment to see whether we're in private session or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're in public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then now move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001 the situation in Mirkovci and in Cair was complicated because of the crisis caused by terrorist attacks and Albanian extremist attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. As you know, the first incident with the terrorist groups took place precisely at the territory of the Mirkovci police station, that comprises also the village of Tanusevci. It is there where the first information about presence of terrorist groups came when they kidnapped or held captive journalists of TV station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it correct that in that area, but in other areas as well, especially Kumanovo, Tetovo, these extremist Albanian groups particularly attacked police station, police patrol, and patrolling the area became increasingly dangerous. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you agree with me, Mr. M-037, when I say that the area of your police station, on the other hand, was of exceptional importance for the overall security of the city of Skopje. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Well, not only Skopje, there is a corridor from the village of Tanusevci to the village of Brest. And on a very short section of the road, certain terrorist groups could use this road to transport certain quantity of weapons, drugs. They could also traffic people. That is the road that is the mountain, Skopska Crna Gora mountain, that would come from Brest to Skopje and Kumanovo; not directly Skopje and Kumanovo, but the entire territory of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the basis of what you said just now in your answer, I can infer, and you tell me whether you agree with this or not, that the crisis areas of Tetovo and Kumanovo and the closeness of the border and the possibility of having all of this linked up, that all of this put together further complicated the security not only of Skopje but all of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. Even from the other side of the Skopska Crna Gora mountain, the village of Matejce is located; and I suppose that the mortar of a larger calibre could even reach and cause damage at the territory of Skopje, specifically Ljubanci and Ljuboten, that part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This kind of security situation, even before the incidents in Ljuboten, brought about a decision passed by the army of Macedonia that they deploy their forces on the Skopska Crna Gora and especially around the village ever Ljuboten. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. There were many members of the army above the village of Ljuboten, above Ljubanci, in general in many positions at the Skopska Crna Gora mountain, and it is considered that they are of vital importance for the defence of the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Because of this overall situation that your area was in, it is with special attention that you received all information that described the state of affairs in Ljuboten itself; not only you, but all of your colleagues, all the policemen in Cair. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In view of this kind of a security situation that you described previously, is it not correct that all of you policemen in the municipality of Cair and in your police station paid particular attention to information about movements of the KLA and the situation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037
utterances.text: Yes. At Ljuboten, since this is the only Albanian village apart from Tanusevci that is very far away, of course, we had valid information that evidence that certain terrorist groups are stationed in the village of Ljuboten, that an improvised infirmary, field hospital was stationed there or under preparation already. And there were information about movements of people who were transporting weapons from Kosovo to Ljuboten using the corridor Tanusevci/Skopska Crna Gora, the entrance into Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters ask that the Judge's microphone is switched off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, I have tried to let you run on to get what you are reaching, but we're now about five minutes over time. I am afraid we must stop there, even though I can see you're still dealing with an important issue. We need to go into public session. Are we in public? Yes. I'm sorry we must interrupt you, and we must now adjourn and we resume tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of May, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
